# PFW-003: No provider rule allows all UDP from anywhere

- **Group:** Provider firewall
- **Severity when it fails:** high
- **Root:** not needed

## Why it matters

UDP has no handshake, so a rule that allows every UDP port from anywhere exposes every UDP service on the host, including ones bound by mistake (DNS resolvers, memcached, game servers) and amplification targets. A wide UDP range is a warning. On a stateless firewall a rule that matches only a source port (OVH's example permits UDP from source port 53) also lets any sender reach every UDP port by choosing that source port; it is reported as a warning, because it is the provider's own advice for DNS replies.

## Verify by hand

```sh
List the inbound UDP rules of the provider firewall and look for a missing port, a range of 1000 ports or more, or a source port with no destination port
```

## How to fix it

Allow only the UDP ports your services use; on OVH, give source port rules a destination port range too where the service allows it (the ephemeral range 32768 to 60999 for replies)

## What a fix can break

Removing a UDP rule a service relies on (WireGuard, Tailscale direct connections, QUIC) cuts that service off or slows it down.
